object_description: staggered linear volume with shed roof
design_condition: The volume is set back and stepped into the slope between existing buildings, using the topography to control height, define two addresses, and form varied outdoor spaces.

positive.statement: The simple, context-responsive volume uses the topography cleverly to create appropriate height development, perceived building lengths, outdoor spaces, and access situations.
The internal street connects the two entrances on two floors, with appropriate entrance areas, atriums, and vertical references enabling good operational processes.
The centrally arranged office and training rooms allow short distances, views, and a high atmospheric density.
The structural concept minimizes supports in the large-span workshops and enables a high level of flexibility of use.
The construction and robust material choices meet the sustainability requirements and enable easy system separation and high flexibility of use.
The low proportion of underground construction volume has a positive impact on construction costs.
The self-confident conceptual approach has the potential to give the educational campus a new, independent expression.

negative.statement: The offset defining the entrance area bears little relation to the existing building.
The hard-surface treatment and tree islands miss the important historical context of the existing building.
The large staircase is understandable topographically but is not convincing in its formulation.
The formal expansion of the cafeteria access area into the district's important open space is hardly conceivable.
The bicycle parking spaces are inexplicably not located at the entrances.
It is doubtful whether the metal facade can integrate into the surrounding historic district; its materialization reinforces the autonomy of the volume.
Access to individual rooms and workshops exclusively through other usable spaces is viewed negatively.
The project still has significant deficiencies in terms of fire protection.
